answer.evidence: The seat spans rows 18-24 and is 8 px wide. Rows 18-21 are a light top plane. Row 22 is a darker front-edge line, and rows 23-24 are darker eave shadow. Below it, 4 px wide legs run down rows 25-30. The backrest (rows 6-11) is a framed panel seen face-on with a light inner band and a dark border. It is a vertical element, so I did not count it as a top surface. The side posts (rows 12-16) join the backrest to the seat. The seat top is 4 rows, which is more than a rim, and it ends in an edge line plus shadow, so the main body reads as three-quarter.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small green chair seen from behind, with 7 distinct colours against 14 for the bench and lamp and 38-40 for the stall and well. Its outline is tinted dark green (0% neutral edge pixels), which is correct and better than the lamp's 100% neutral line. The shading is shallow, though: about 3 steps (a light top-rail edge, a mid green body and a dark outline). There is no grain, plank texture or per-part highlight on the backrest slats or legs, so it reads as a flat-filled sticker next to the bench's multi-tone wood. The 5x5 flat-fill coverage is 0% only because the piece is thin. Per-tile density is 0 because the piece is smaller than a tile, so I judged by eye, and it looks thinner and flatter than the bench reference. A careful artist would not accept it beside the bench without adding more tonal steps and wood grain.
